answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a bonded identity ledger. Before an agent may transact it locks a bond that is slashed the moment its cluster is detected: auditors flag accounts that share a cipher fingerprint, reuse a signing key, or cluster on the same statistical ridge of activity timing. Reputation then accrues only through sustained honest work across epochs, so an attacker cannot spin up a lotus of fresh identities overnight; each new node costs a fresh bond, and slashed funds are redistributed to honest validators.
